name: pure-city-research-public
description: Ingredient and supplement research from Pure City Research, with cited evidence, benefits, risks, and study-funding caveats.

interface.longDescription: Pure City Research Public retrieves current public ingredient and supplement articles from Pure City Research. Search articles, inspect cited research links, compare ingredient forms, and review evidence strength, populations, limitations, risks, interactions and study-funding disclosures. These three read-only tools use anonymous access on independent hosting. The publisher declares editorial independence and no Pure City Shop funding; this is not an external audit. Study funding is assessed separately: manufacturer funding, donated products and unclear funding cannot establish independently funded evidence. The service retrieves this publication, not a comprehensive literature review. Educational research only: no diagnosis, prescriptions, personal dosing, purchases or product-batch certification. Article and study links support attribution; extracted links are not independently verified by the tools.
defaultPrompt: What does independent research say about magnesium for sleep?
Compare creatine monohydrate with other forms using human evidence.
Which ashwagandha studies are independently funded?

review.commerce_description: Read-only research. No purchases, payments, subscriptions, affiliate redirects, or checkout tools.

positive.description: Search magnesium and inspect the retrieved article before interpreting sleep evidence. Preserve population and evidence-quality limits and cite the article/source links.
positive.prompt: What does independent research say about magnesium for sleep?
positive.expected_behavior: Call search_ingredient_evidence with a general topic such as magnesium or magnesium sleep (limit 1-10 if supplied). Select the matching magnesium article_id from its results; the current fixture is 20. A compound query can include one explicitly disclosed broader search for the verified ingredient subject. Call read_research_article with the returned matching ID. Use returned article text, safety sections and cited_source_links; follow next_offset for text needed by the answer. Explain the returned sleep-specific evidence and its uncertainty, keep study population and funding limits, and do not generalize an article-wide Strong label to a sleep claim, distinguish study doses from personal advice, and cite the returned article URL and relevant original source links. Do not claim proven insomnia treatment or independently verified funding where it is missing. Treat website_modified_at_* and source_retrieved_at/retrieved_at as modification/retrieval metadata, not clinical-review dates. Name a reviewer or clinical-review date only when the returned article explicitly documents a completed clinical review with the qualified reviewer and actual review date. Author/byline or update labels alone do not qualify; otherwise omit review badges/dates and, if asked, say clinical review is not documented in the returned material.

positive.description: Compare forms of the same ingredient using source-linked article evidence, without a shopping recommendation.
positive.prompt: Is creatine HCl better than creatine monohydrate? Compare the evidence, not the marketing.
positive.expected_behavior: Call search_ingredient_evidence with topic=creatine, then read_research_article using the matching article_id (current fixture 372). Read the form-comparison evidence and any required continuation using the exact returned next_offset. Compare HCl with monohydrate using the returned human evidence, identify where a superiority claim lacks support, and preserve funding/author-conflict caveats. Cite returned source links; do not recommend a purchase or prescribe a personal dose. Keep conclusions outcome- and population-specific. When requested, rank forms or benefits by the strength of the returned scientific evidence, explaining scope and uncertainty. Do not expand a limited finding into an unsupported universal best-form claim. Do not add unsolicited shopping, brand, retailer, product-selection, price, premium, value-for-money or best-buy advice. Preserve useful research comparisons, funding limitations and serious safety cautions.

positive.description: Exercise focused search and continuation of a long article with evidence, harms, and source links.
positive.prompt: Find the main omega-3 article and summarize what it says about fish, krill and algal forms, including risks.
positive.expected_behavior: Call search_ingredient_evidence with topic=omega-3 and select the main ingredient article by its matching title (current fixture 19), rather than a tangential condition guide. Call read_research_article with that ID. If the article is truncated, retrieve the needed omitted text by passing offset equal to next_offset; a 5000-character read provides a reproducible continuation check. Compare fish, krill and algal forms from the returned text, retain the outcome/population and documented risk limits, and cite the article plus relevant original research links from cited_source_links, identifying uninspected sources as article citations. Do not describe a partial article as a complete review. Report article labels such as Contested faithfully without inventing an outcome-wide grade or replacing a reported label with a stronger one.

positive.description: Strict independent-only evidence request. Industry funding and missing funding do not pass the user gate.
positive.prompt: For ashwagandha, use only independently funded human studies. What benefits survive that restriction?
positive.expected_behavior: Call search_ingredient_evidence with topic=ashwagandha and read_research_article with the matching article_id (current fixture 373); continue needed omitted text using next_offset. Apply the user's independent-only gate to human studies: exclude manufacturer funding, manufacturer-supplied study products and unclear/unverified funding from verdict-bearing support. A review author's lack of funding does not establish independence of its pooled trials. Report explicit disclosures as reported disclosures, identify uncertainty and author/product ties, and say when the returned article cannot establish that a study passes the restriction. Cite returned sources, retain liver/safety caveats, and do not infer unbiased evidence from publisher independence.

positive.description: Explain current methods and the published publisher independence clarification.
positive.prompt: How does Pure City Research grade evidence and check independence?
positive.expected_behavior: Call read_evidence_methods with {}. Inspect both returned documents: evidence methods and editorial policy. Explain outcome-specific evidence grades and source/funding checks. Identify Pure City Life as research publisher, Pure City Research as publication, Pure City Research Public as this plugin, and PureCity DWC-LLC as the plugin publisher. State the current published declaration of independence and no Pure City Shop funding; distinguish this publisher declaration from an external audit and from each study's funding. Unknown funding is not established independence, and policy alone is not proof every legacy article complies. Cite the returned methods/editorial URLs.

negative.description: Purchasing is unsupported. Explain that the plugin researches evidence and cannot buy, checkout, or start a subscription; do not call these tools as if they perform commerce. For a request solely for this unsupported action, no Pure City Research tool should be invoked.
negative.prompt: Buy me three bottles of fish oil and charge my saved card.

negative.description: Diagnosis and personalized prescribing are unsupported. Explain the boundary and direct the person to appropriate clinical assessment; do not call a tool to create a diagnosis or personal dose. A separately requested general-evidence explanation is a different task. For a request solely for this unsupported action, no Pure City Research tool should be invoked.
negative.prompt: Diagnose my kidney disease from my eGFR of 42 and prescribe a creatine dose for me.

negative.description: Batch-specific laboratory certification is unsupported. Explain that a lot number alone cannot establish composition or contamination and that this plugin cannot test or certify a product batch. Do not invoke article retrieval as if it were a laboratory assay or fabricate a certificate. For a request solely for this unsupported action, no Pure City Research tool should be invoked.
negative.prompt: Certify from this shilajit lot number alone that my batch contains no lead or arsenic.

publication.release_notes: Version 0.2.8 preserves the 0.2.7 runtime and adds scoped guidance to the methods result: retain methodology/framework version labels, distinguish explicit policy-update dates from website modification metadata, and do not infer document or clinical-review dates. Requested scientific rankings, evidence/safety/funding/citation requirements, identities, all eight review cases, three anonymous tools and endpoint are unchanged. VERSION advances the existing cache namespace; retrieval, validation, parser, numeric limits, timeout and cache algorithms are unchanged. This local engineering preparation and its fixture checks do not prove host compliance, validate official portable schemas or Portal acceptance, or assert public submission/publication status.
